headline: 10 crude bombs explode in Dhaka; empty bus set on fire in Kafrul
summary: An auto-rickshaw driver was injured in a series of blasts across six areas of the capital, while an empty bus was torched near a police station.
details: A total of 10 crude bombs exploded across six different locations in Dhaka on Friday, followed by an incident where an empty bus was set on fire in front of the Kafrul police station.

The blasts occurred between noon and 11 PM, with locations including Jatrabari, Malibagh, Agargaon, Mohakhali, Babubazar, and Moghbazar. In Jatrabari, an auto-rickshaw driver named Ibadur Rahman was injured and sent to Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
Police suspect that most of the bombs were thrown from flyovers, except for those in Agargaon. Two blasts were reported near the Malibagh Railgate and the BTV building in Rampura.
The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) stated that the identities of those responsible have not yet been confirmed, but they are using intelligence and IT data to identify and arrest the perpetrators.

Police noted that banned Awami League members have recently attempted flash marches after Friday prayers. On September 11, such a march in Gulshan led to blasts and clashes with police, resulting in 83 arrests.
The unrest follows recent legal developments, including the International Crimes Tribunal-2's death sentence for former Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Kader and six others on Tuesday.
caption:
10 crude bombs explode across Dhaka in a single day. An auto-rickshaw driver injured and a bus torched.

A total of 10 crude bombs exploded across six different locations in Dhaka on Friday, followed by an incident where an empty bus was set on fire in front of the Kafrul police station.

The blasts occurred between noon and 11 PM, with locations including Jatrabari, Malibagh, Agargaon, Mohakhali, Babubazar, and Moghbazar. In Jatrabari, an auto-rickshaw driver named Ibadur Rahman was injured and sent to Dhaka Medical College Hospital.

Police suspect that most of the bombs were thrown from flyovers, except for those in Agargaon. Two blasts were reported near the Malibagh Railgate and the BTV building in Rampura.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) stated that the identities of those responsible have not yet been confirmed, but they are using intelligence and IT data to identify and arrest the perpetrators.

Police noted that banned Awami League members have recently attempted flash marches after Friday prayers. On September 11, such a march in Gulshan led to blasts and clashes with police, resulting in 83 arrests.

The unrest follows recent legal developments, including the International Crimes Tribunal-2's death sentence for former Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Kader and six others on Tuesday.

headline: Dengue crisis: Dengue cases surpass 10,000 in Khulna Division as hospitals overflow
summary: With 747 patients hospitalized in a single day, healthcare facilities are struggling to keep up with the surge in infections.
details: Dengue infections have reached a critical point in Bangladesh, with cases in the Khulna Division alone surpassing 10,000.
The surge has put immense pressure on the healthcare system, with hospitals reporting that they are overwhelmed by the number of patients.
In a recent 24-hour period, 747 patients were admitted to hospitals for dengue treatment, although no deaths were reported during that specific window.
Health officials are concerned about the risk of further spikes in infections as October looms, urging the public to maintain strict precautions against mosquito breeding.
